title: Photolabile oligonucleotides with topological light gradients enable spatially resolved single-cell transcriptomics and epigenomics - Nature Biotechnology
text:
AbstractWe introduce scSTAMP-seq (single-cell spatial transcriptomic and multiomic profiling), a modular light-encoded barcoding strategy that preserves spatial information while leveraging standard single-cell platforms. scSTAMP-seq labels live and fixed cells with cholesterol-conjugated, photocleavable hashtag oligonucleotides, followed by patterned light exposure that ‘stamps’ spatial coordinates onto individual cells before single-cell multiome sequencing. Here we apply scSTAMP-seq to human embryoids showing how spatial organization and epigenetic states coregulate cellular programs in heterogeneous biological systems.

Custom code for analyzing scSTAMP-seq data and the accompanying documentation are available on GitHub (https://github.com/deylabucsb/scSTAMP-seq).

Additional informationPublisher’s note Springer Nature remains neutral with regard to jurisdictional claims in published maps and institutional affiliations.Extended dataExtended Data Fig. 1 Design of different PHO variants and downstream capture in single-cell sequencing.a, Schematic of the components of PHO and MPO molecules. Both the ‘inner’ and ‘outer’ DNA sequences of PHOs contain a PCR handle for downstream amplification, an ‘inner’- and ‘outer’-specific barcode, a 6-nucleotide UMI to count individual molecules, and a poly-A capture sequence. The ‘inner’ PCR handle also hybridizes to a complementary sequence on the CMO anchor to embed in cell membranes. MPOs resemble the ‘inner’ PHO sequence but contain an additional multiplex identification sequence to distinguish MPOs from PHOs. b, Schematic of three PHO fluorophore conjugation schemes. PHOs can be conjugated to ‘inner’ and ‘outer’ fluorophores, an ‘outer’ fluorophore alone, or no fluorophore to enable visualization of PHO cleavage prior to downstream sequencing. c, Schematic of PHO library preparation. Uncleaved and cleaved PHOs are first copied using a primer containing a T7 promoter (teal), RA5 handle (purple), cell-specific barcode, UMI (magenta), and polyT capture sequence (gray). Following second strand synthesis, PHO-derived molecules are separated from endogenous cDNA by SPRI bead purification. An RA3 handle primer (yellow) together with either an ‘inner’ (blue) or ‘outer’ (red) adapter and an Illumina P5 primer (indigo) are then used to amplify and extend PHO molecules by PCR. Finally, a second PCR using a primer containing an Illumina P7 (brown), sample index sequence (tan), and RA3 adapter, along with the same RA5-P5 primer from the previous step are used to generate the final Illumina sequencing libraries.Extended Data Fig. 2 Patterned illumination of PHO labeled cells.a, Images of user-defined patterned illumination over live cells. DMD-projected photomasks (left) for a binary UCSB logo (top) and a linear gradient (bottom) used to illuminate live cells labeled with an ‘inner’ Cy3- and ‘outer’ Cy5-conjugated PHO. Corresponding ‘inner’ Cy3 (middle) and ‘outer’ Cy5 (right) fluorescence images are shown after illumination. Scale bars, 100 µm. b, Normalized Cy5 over Cy3 fluorescence as a function of DLP light intensity for the linear gradient at the specified illumination times in the time lapse shown in Supplementary Video 2. c,d, 365-nm LED floodlight illumination over live cells. Representative Cy3 and Cy5 PHO fluorescence images (c) and corresponding quantification of normalized Cy5 fluorescence (d) following 0-, 1-, or 10-minute floodlight illumination. Scale bars, 100 µm. In panel d, data represents three imaging fields of view collected from each independently treated culture plate. Center lines indicate the median, boxes denote the interquartile range (IQR), and whiskers extend to the minimum and maximum values that are within 1.5x IQR. One culture plate was analyzed per illumination condition. e, DMDs can label individual cells with user-defined illumination. Representative composite fluorescence images of an ‘outer’ Cy5-conjugated PHO-labeled (gray) co-culture containing wildtype U2OS and mCherry-expressing HeLa cells (orange). DMD-generated photomasks (magenta) were generated by thresholding on mCherry-positive HeLa cells. Scale bars, 100 µm. f, Violin plot of the ratio of Cy5 fluorescence after and before illumination for HeLa and U2OS cells. Individual points represent single cells (HeLa, n = 79 cells; U2OS, n = 552 cells; N = 631 total cells) quantified from one well of a 96-well plate. *** indicates a statistically significant difference between distributions (p < 2.22e-16, Mann-Whitney U test).Source dataExtended Data Fig. 3 Validation and characterization of scSTAMP-seq.a, Bioanalyzer trace of the spatial PHO Illumina library generated by scSTAMP-seq shows the expected size of the library after enrichment with 3.2x SPRI beads with 1.8x 100% isopropanol following the amplification protocol described in Extended Data Fig. 1c. b, Comparison of the transcriptome obtained from scSTAMP-seq to scRNA-seq. Violin plots show the number of genes and unique transcripts detected per cell. Individual points represent single cells. Center lines indicate the median and boxes denote the interquartile range (IQR). Data were analyzed after quality-control filtering of scRNA-seq (n = 111 cells) and scSTAMP-seq (n = 81 cells). c, UV illumination does not alter the endogenous transcriptome in plate-based scSTAMP-seq. Scatterplot compares normalized gene expression between cells exposed to no light and saturating UV illumination required for complete PHO cleavage (Pearson’s r = 0.997, Spearman’s ρ = 0.987). Individual points represent genes (n = 14,983 genes). d, Principal component analysis (PCA) of the transcriptome of individual cells exposed to no illumination (open points; n = 36 cells) and saturating UV illumination (filled points; n = 46 cells) processed by scSTAMP-seq (N = 82 total cells). e, Volcano plot of differential gene expression between illuminated and non-illuminated cells. Each point represents a gene. The x-axis indicates the log2 fold change in expression between conditions, and the y-axis indicates the -log10 p-value. Genes meeting both statistical significance (p < 0.05) and a fold-change threshold (|log2 FC | > 0.5) are highlighted in red, with all other genes shown in gray. A total of 9,518 genes were tested. f, Representative fluorescence images show the retention of PHOs on live cell membranes over time. Scale bars, 100 µm. g, Quantification of membrane fluorescence intensity over time. Points represent the median fluorescence intensity from three imaging fields of view collected from each independently treated culture plate, and error bars indicate the median absolute deviation. The measured decay corresponds to an estimated half-life of PHOs on cell membranes to be 9.05 hours, defining the time window for live-cell scSTAMP-seq experiments. h, Biotin-streptavidin-mediated anchoring of PHOs on cell membranes. Schematic illustrating cell surface biotinylation and anchoring PHOs to cell membranes. Biotin is conjugated to the amine group of cell surface proteins, represented as red, blue, and green objects. Redesigned anchor oligos are conjugated to biotin in place of cholesterol, which is then bound to streptavidin after a 10-minute incubation. The biotinylated PHO and streptavidin complex are then introduced to samples, which binds the biotinylated cell membrane proteins. i, Representative fluorescence image of live HeLa cells labeled using the biotin-streptavidin anchoring strategy with Cy5-conjugated PHOs. Scale bar, 100 µm.Source dataExtended Data Fig. 4 scSTAMP-seq enables spatial transcriptomic profiling of fixed cells.a, Representative DIC and Cy5 fluorescence images of HeLa cells that were either not treated with DSP (Unfixed live cells) or treated with DSP (DSP-fixed cells), comparing live (left) and fixed (right) samples. Cy5 fluorescence indicates membrane-bound PHOs before (top) and after (bottom) light exposure. Loss of Cy5 fluorescence following illumination demonstrates light-induced PHO cleavage in both live and fixed samples. Scale bars, 100 µm. b, Scatterplot comparing normalized gene expression between live and DSP-treated fixed cells (Pearson’s r = 0.967, Spearman’s ρ = 0.860). Individual points represent genes (n = 15,895 genes). c, Principal component analysis (PCA) of the transcriptome of live (open points; n = 64 cells) and DSP-treated fixed (filled points; n = 88 cells) cells processed by scSTAMP-seq (N = 152 total cells). d, Volcano plot of differential gene expression between live and DSP-treated fixed cells in scSTAMP-seq. Each point represents a gene. The x-axis indicates the log2 fold change in expression between the two conditions, and the y-axis indicates the -log10 p-value. Genes meeting both statistical significance (p < 0.05) and a fold-change threshold (|log2 FC | > 0.5) are highlighted in red, with all other genes shown in gray. Individual points represent single cells. After quality-control filtering, panels include 0 s (n = 36 cells), 1.5 s (n = 41 cells), 4.5 s (n = 44 cells), 13.5 s (n = 42 cells), and 18 s (n = 32 cells) illumination conditions (N = 195 total cells). b, Heatmap of normalized ‘outer’-to-‘inner’ PHO sequencing read counts for PHO1-6 across the same 195 single cells shown in panel (a).Source dataExtended Data Fig. 6 Sequential rounds of optical labeling increase the spatial resolution of scSTAMP-seq.a, Top row – DMD-generated binary photomasks applied sequentially during three rounds of optical labeling with PHO1, PHO2, and PHO3. Middle row – fluorescence images of cells labeled with Cy5-conjugated PHO1 (left), FAM-conjugated PHO2 (middle), and Cy3-conjugated PHO3 (right) following each round of patterned illumination. Bottom row – composite false-color overlays of the three PHO fluorophores after each labeling round. Scale bars, 100 µm. b, Three-dimensional scatterplot of normalized PHO1, PHO2, and PHO3 fluorescence intensities for single cells segmented from the images shown in panel (a). Forty cells were manually selected from each spatial quadrant (Q1-Q4; N = 160 total cells) using Fiji. Individual cells are colored according to their assigned spatial quadrant based on the combination of their fluorescence intensities. Dashed lines indicate the mean fluorescence intensity of each PHO within each quadrant.Source dataExtended Data Fig. 7 Design and validation of PHO-v2 and bridging oligonucleotides (BO) for sequential spatial encoding with memory.a, Schematic of the PHO-v2 and bridging oligonucleotide (BO) designs. PHO-v2 sequences are modified slightly from the original sequence to incorporate an ‘inner’ bridge handle downstream of the ‘inner’ polyA sequence to enable hybridization with BOs. BOs are complementary to both the PHO-v2 ‘inner’ bridge handle and the ‘outer’ PCR handle, thereby preventing release of the cleaved ‘outer’ PHO-v2 sequence after illumination. b, BO hybridization prevents release of the ‘outer’ PHO-v2 sequence during photocleavage. Representative fluorescence images of cells labeled with an ‘outer’ Cy5-conjugated PHO-v2 molecules (grayscale) before illumination (left), during patterned illumination (middle), and after illumination (right). In the absence of BOs (top), Cy5 fluorescence is lost from illuminated regions following photocleavage, indicating release of the ‘outer’ PHO-v2 sequence. In the presence of BOs (bottom), Cy5 fluorescence is retained after illumination, demonstrating that BO hybridization preserves the ‘outer’ PHO-v2 sequence from release. Scale bars, 100 µm. c, Sequential optical labeling enables combinatorial spatial encoding in the presence of BOs. Cells were labeled in three successive rounds with uniquely barcoded PHO-v2 molecules (PHO1-PHO3), each conjugated to a distinct fluorophore, followed by BO addition after each illumination round. For each round, the top row shows the programmed illumination pattern, and the bottom row shows the corresponding experimental fluorescence image. Black, gray, and white pixels indicate no, intermediate, and saturating illumination levels, respectively. Composite images demonstrate the unique RGB fluorescence combinations generated by sequential rounds of optical labeling for two illumination schemes (2 x 4 and 3 x 6), illustrating how BO-mediated preservation of previous labeling patterns enables exponential expansion of spatial encoding capacity. Scale bars, 100 µm.Extended Data Fig. 8 Droplet-based spatially-resolved transcriptomics using scSTAMP-seq.a, Schematic of PHO library preparation for droplet-based scSTAMP-seq using the 10x Genomics platform. Uncleaved and cleaved PHOs are copied using a polyT capture primer (gray), which also contains an Illumina TruSeq Read 1 sequence (black), a cell specific 10x barcode (green), and a UMI (orange). Following the extension of these molecules using a template switching oligo (TSO; teal), PHO-derived molecules are separated from endogenous mRNA-derived cDNA using SPRI beads.
